method: Independent static PE, entry-path and instruction/data-flow review using Rizin and LLVM objdump; cleave facts includes decoded strings. No specimen execution or endpoint contact.
shared_evidence: The complete .text bytes at file offsets 0x1000..0x2fff are identical in all three samples; the entry at VA 0x402674 calls main at VA 0x401cb0.
Configuration dword VA 0x404120 is 3. The selected branch at VA 0x401f75 calls the self-copy routine at VA 0x401900, followed by shell cleanup at VA 0x401390.

The self-copy routine generates a GUID-derived name, constructs a destination executable path, calls RegCreateKeyA and RegSetValueExA, reads its current image with CRT I/O, patches a copy, writes it with fwrite, and passes the copied path to CreateProcessA at VA 0x401b7e.
The cleanup routine gets the current image pathname and its short form, reads COMSPEC, builds /c del with redirection to nul, and calls CreateProcessA at VA 0x4014b8.

Alternate installer paths at VA 0x402460 extract resource DLL/101 and write it through VA 0x4023c0. VA 0x401260 deletes and replaces LanmanServer Parameters ServiceDLL. VA 0x401150 creates a target process, allocates remote storage, writes the DLL path, resolves LoadLibraryA, and passes that function and remote buffer to CreateRemoteThread at VA 0x40123d.
Fixed self-copy patch offsets (including 0x6a0 and 0x3058) belong to an earlier file layout. The present images retain malicious code but should not be represented as proven successful infections.

evidence: The entire 40960-byte .rsrc section is zero. Its resource directory and DLL payload are absent; additional nonstandard sections are also zero-filled.
The outer loader retains readable Active Setup, LanmanServer, injection-target and shell-cleanup data plus the corresponding code. No working embedded DDoS payload remains.

samples.identification: StormAttack loader with a damaged packet-tasked DDoS DLL
samples.marker_note: StormAttack loader and damaged DDoS DLL: no change
evidence: A valid DLL/101 resource entry points to 39936 bytes at file offset 0x5060. Its DLL entry VA 0x1000741a reaches initialization at VA 0x10007176 and worker setup for VA 0x10006922.

VA 0x10006974 builds the connection and sends host information; VA 0x10006ac9 processes the connected socket. The call at VA 0x10006b45 targets the recv import (Winsock ordinal 16), copies a 0x528-byte record and dispatches its leading command dword.

VA 0x100022b6 calls WSASocketA(AF_INET, SOCK_RAW, IPPROTO_UDP), and VA 0x100022d5 enables IP_HDRINCL. VA 0x1000236b calls sendto (Winsock ordinal 20) twelve times per burst, sleeps, and repeats until the global stop flag changes.

Many strings were replaced with equal-length random-looking text. Executable bytes are also damaged: examples at VA 0x10006907 and VA 0x100070cd break portions of the launch/dispatch paths. No runtime decoder restoring those bytes was found.

The Active Setup and LanmanServer path strings are replaced, and the outer kernel32 lookup target is damaged. Accordingly, the specific persistence traits do not fire on this parent. Remaining resource/injection/cleanup code and the child flood/dispatch code establish malicious purpose without asserting successful persistence, downloading or execution.

samples.identification: StormAttack loader carrying an erased-code DLL
samples.marker_note: StormAttack loader (erased DLL code): no change
evidence: The resource tree and embedded PE header at file offset 0x5060 remain, as do Storm banners, packet-format text and HTTP/API references.

The embedded DLL executable routines and imports have been zeroed. The byte range corresponding to the surviving DDoS code in the second sample is zero; no flood or packet-control hostile traits fire on this child.
Outer Active Setup, service-DLL replacement, injection and shell-cleanup routines remain. HTTP and API strings in the erased child establish references only, not a working downloader.

trait_changes: No YAML changes. Existing traits correctly describe retained code/API profiles, including damaged descendants; a missing resource or erased child does not erase the surviving malicious installer code.
attribution_limits: Code and family banners support StormAttack. Collector filename labels and sandbox/ML scores were not proof; no Remcos or WannaCry behavior was established.
verification: All three original samples scanned and rescanned with atomscan; final trait IDs and severities equal their initial sets. No YAML changed, so make validate was not run as instructed.
